intro: Pooling reduces spatial resolution by retaining the strongest activation inside each local window.
task: Return two-dimensional max pooling for a supplied window shape and shared integer stride, with no padding.
requirements: image is a nonempty finite matrix. window is a two-element list or tuple of positive integers that fits inside the image.
stride is a positive integer. Boolean window sizes and strides are invalid.
Only full windows count; discard incomplete trailing windows. Return a NumPy matrix. Negative maxima must remain negative.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: For each axis the output count is floor((input - window) / stride) + 1.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Take the actual window maximum, even when every entry is below zero.

explanation: Max pooling keeps a local extreme while discarding precise within-window position. This changes the representation and spatial resolution without learning a kernel.
Output positions begin at zero and advance by stride while the complete window fits. Initializing a maximum to zero would incorrectly erase all-negative windows.
Move the largest pixel within a non-overlapping window and compare outputs. Then move it across a window boundary to identify the limit of this local invariance.
